headings: LITTLE LESSONS FROM THE FOUR LAWS
core_concepts: IN THIS BOOK,I have introduced a four-step model for human behavior: cue, craving, response, reward
In this section, I have compiled some lessons (and a few bits of common sense) that are confirmed by the model
Happiness is simply the absence of desire
However, happiness is fleeting because a new desire always comes along
It is the of pleasure that we chase
Peace occurs when you don’t turn your observations into problems
Craving is about wanting to fix everything
With a big enough you can overcome any
Being curious is better than being smart
We can only be rational and logical we have been emotional
mechanisms_or_explanations: This framework not only teaches us how to create new habits but also reveals some interesting insights about human behavior
The purpose of these examples is to clarify just how useful and wide-ranging this framework is when describing human behavior
A craving is created when you assign meaning to a cue
When you observe a cue, but do not desire to change your state, you are content with the current situation
It arrives when you have no urge to feel differently
Happiness is the state you enter when you no longer want to change your state
However, happiness is fleeting because a new desire always comes along
At the time of action, we do not know what it will be like to attain that image (or even if it will satisfy us)
This is what the Austrian neurologist Victor Frankl meant when he said that happiness cannot be pursued, it must ensue
Peace occurs when you don’t turn your observations into problems
The first step in any behavior is observation
If you do not desire to act on what you observe, then you are at peace
critical_qualifiers: This framework not only teaches us how to create new habits but also reveals some interesting insights about human behavior
Your brain constructs an emotion or feeling to describe your current situation, and that means a craving can only occur after you have noticed an opportunity
When you observe a cue, but do not desire to change your state, you are content with the current situation
Happiness is not about the achievement of pleasure (which is joy or satisfaction), but about the lack of desire
However, happiness is fleeting because a new desire always comes along
With a big enough you can overcome any
Friedrich Nietzsche, the German philosopher and poet, famously wrote, “He who has a why to live for can bear almost any how.” This phrase harbors an important truth about human behavior
Great craving can power great action—even when friction is high
In fact, people with damage to emotional centers of the brain can list many reasons for taking action but still will not act because they do not have emotions to drive them
We can only be rational and logical we have been emotional
important_examples: The purpose of these examples is to clarify just how useful and wide-ranging this framework is when describing human behavior
Once you understand the model, you’ll see examples of it everywhere
For example, if you expect to get $10 and get $100, you feel great
key_entities_or_numbers: Our second response—the slow, conscious portion of the brain—is the part that does the “thinking.” Psychologists refer to this as System 1 (feelings and rapid judgments) versus System 2 (rational analysis)
The feeling comes first (System 1); the rationality only intervenes later (System 2)
For example, if you expect to get $10 and get $100, you feel great
If you expect to get $100 and get $10, you feel disappointed
